title: The Chamber Office and the Locked Archive: Mises from Lemberg to West End Avenue
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Lemberg, and the Name the Emperor Gave

stops.name: Lemberg, born three months after the ennoblement
stops.date_confidence: Attested. Birth date and place are given by the University of Vienna Memorial Book (gedenkbuch.univie.ac.at) and by English Wikipedia; the ennoblement of Mayer Rachmiel Mises in 1881 is attested by mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time'. The coordinate is the Lviv city point, not a house address: no source consulted names the street.
stops.campa: In Lemberg, capital of Austro-Hungarian Galicia, a son is born to the railway engineer Arthur von Mises and his wife Adele, born Landau. Three months earlier Franz Joseph raised the boy's great-grandfather Mayer Rachmiel Mises to hereditary nobility, so the child is entered in the register as Ludwig Heinrich Edler von Mises: four generations of Galician Jewish trade converted, by an imperial signature, into a particle in front of a surname. The empire that grants the name has thirty-seven years left to run.
sources: University of Vienna Memorial Book (gedenkbuch.univie.ac.at), Mises entry
mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time'
suggested_refs: The 1881 patent of nobility granted to Mayer Rachmiel Mises by Franz Joseph

stops.name: Wollzeile, the family follows the railways west
stops.date_confidence: Year uncertain: mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time', gives the relocation as 1889 or 1892 without deciding, and 1889 is used here only to order the segment. The addresses Elisabethgasse 3, Friedrichstrasse 4 and Wollzeile 24 are attested from the same source; the pin is Wollzeile 24 (48.2081, 16.3768, Nominatim), the address Mises himself later occupied, not necessarily the first the family took.
stops.campa: Arthur von Mises takes a post with the Ministry of Railways and moves the household west out of Galicia to the imperial capital. The family lives at a succession of inner-city addresses, Elisabethgasse, Friedrichstrasse, and at last Wollzeile 24, a few minutes on foot from the cathedral. Ludwig is eight, or he is eleven; the record does not settle it. What the move does settle is that he will be raised a Viennese and not a Galician, in the city where the theory he will spend sixty years defending has already been written down by a man he has not yet heard of.
sources: mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time'
suggested_refs: Vienna address records for the Mises household, Elisabethgasse 3, Friedrichstrasse 4, Wollzeile 24

stops.name: Akademisches Gymnasium, the eight years of Latin
stops.date_confidence: Entry in 1892 attested by mises.org, 'Who Was Ludwig von Mises?'; the month is conventional for a Gymnasium year and is not separately attested. Coordinate corrected to Beethovenplatz 1, 1010 Wien (48.2015, 16.3766, OpenStreetMap/Nominatim). The Kelsen friendship comes from English Wikipedia and the dossier, not from a school register consulted here.
stops.campa: He enters the Akademisches Gymnasium on Beethovenplatz, the humanistic school of the Viennese bourgeoisie: Latin, Greek, history, and the habit of construing a text word by word before permitting yourself to argue with it. Among his classmates is Hans Kelsen, who will draft the Austrian constitution, be driven out of Europe in the same decade as Mises, and end up lecturing beside him again on a lake in Switzerland. For eight years the two boys sit under the same curriculum in the same rooms, learning to take a sentence apart.
suggested_refs: The Akademisches Gymnasium, Beethovenplatz 1, Vienna, and its enrolment registers for 1892-1900

segments.name: The University, Menger, and the Chamber

stops.name: University of Vienna, the law faculty
stops.date_confidence: Enrolment in 1900 in law and government science attested by mises.org, 'Who Was Ludwig von Mises?'; October is the conventional start of the Austrian academic year and is not separately attested. The Galician landlord-and-peasant student study is attested by English Wikipedia and the dossier's education section.
stops.campa: He matriculates in the faculty of law and government science, which in Vienna means jurisprudence, administration, and economics taught together as the training of imperial officials. He arrives a historicist, persuaded like nearly everyone of his generation that economic life is a matter of national circumstance and legislative will, and he writes a student study of landlord and peasant relations in the Galicia he was born in and no longer lives in. The conversion has not happened yet.
suggested_refs: Mises's student study of landlord-peasant relations in Galicia

stops.name: Halberstadt, the father does not come out of surgery
stops.date_confidence: Year and place attested by mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time'; month and day are unattested and defaulted. The coordinate is the Halberstadt town point: no source consulted names the hospital, the surgeon, or the procedure. Arthur von Mises's exact age at death is not stated in the sources reached.
stops.campa: Arthur von Mises goes into surgery in Halberstadt, in Prussian Saxony, and does not come out of it. Ludwig is twenty-two and halfway through the law faculty. His mother Adele keeps the Vienna household and the charitable obligations of a family that still has money and no longer has its engineer, and the son who will spend his life writing about how men choose under scarcity acquires at one stroke an income he did not earn and a household to think about. No source consulted names the operation, the hospital, or the ward.
sources: mises.org, 'Ludwig von Mises and the Vienna of His Time'
suggested_refs: Halberstadt municipal death records for 1903

stops.name: University of Vienna, reading Menger's Grundsatze
stops.date_confidence: Circa 1903, and the whole of it rests on Mises's own retrospective account in Notes and Recollections; no contemporary document places the reading in a particular month or year. The month here is purely an ordering device, set after his father's death in the same year, and carries no evidential weight. The stop sits at the university pin because that is where he was enrolled, not because the reading is recorded as happening in the building.
stops.campa: In his third year he reads Carl Menger's Grundsatze der Volkswirthschaftslehre, published in Vienna thirty years before he opened it, and by his own later account the book makes an economist of him. Value is not a property of the thing. It is the rank a particular person assigns to the next unit of it. Everything Mises writes afterward is built on that proposition and on the man who set it down, who is at this moment still alive across the city, retired early from his chair and teaching nobody at all.
stops.quote: He foresaw all the horrors which we are experiencing today. He knew the consequences of the world's turning away from true Liberalism and Capitalism.
stops.quote_source: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. IV, on Carl Menger; written 1940, 'today' meaning 1940
sources: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. IV
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, Grundsatze der Volkswirthschaftslehre (Vienna, 1871)

stops.name: University of Vienna, Bohm-Bawerk's seminar
stops.date_confidence: Attendance from 1904 attested in the dossier from Mises's Notes and Recollections; month defaulted to the start of the academic year. The presence of Schumpeter, Bauer and Hilferding in the same seminar is standard in the literature on the Austrian School and is carried here from the dossier rather than from a seminar register.
stops.campa: From 1904 he sits in Eugen von Bohm-Bawerk's seminar, the room in which Austrian economics is argued out loud rather than read. Around the table are Joseph Schumpeter, Otto Bauer, and Rudolf Hilferding: three men who will spend their working lives on the far side of every question Mises cares about. Bauer will lead Austrian Marxism, Hilferding will write the theory of finance capital and serve twice as a German finance minister. Mises will fight all three in print for forty years. They learn the method together first, in this room, as students.
stops.quote: Bohm-Bawerk was a brilliant seminar leader. He did not think of himself as a teacher, but as a chairman who occasionally also participated in the discussion.
stops.quote_source: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. IV, 'The Austrian School of Economics'
sources: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. IV
Dossier, teachers and intellectual conversion section
suggested_refs: Bohm-Bawerk's Vienna seminar, 1904-1914

stops.name: University of Vienna, the doctorate in law
stops.date_confidence: Attested: mises.org, 'Who Was Ludwig von Mises?', gives February 1906; the dossier gives 20 February 1906 and the day is carried from the dossier without independent confirmation. Entry into the state financial administration in 1906 is a reconstruction from the same source's general statement, with no appointment document consulted.
stops.campa: The Dr. jur. is conferred in February. It is a law degree, because there is no doctorate in economics in Austria to take, and there will be no salaried economics chair for him anywhere in the country for the next twenty-eight years. He goes into the financial administration of the state and drafts tax and currency memoranda for an empire that will shortly need all of them and act on none. The career opens exactly the way a well-born Viennese law doctor's career is supposed to open, and then declines to continue that way.
suggested_refs: University of Vienna promotion records, February 1906

stops.name: The Chamber of Commerce, Vienna: the salaried post
stops.date_confidence: Attested by mises.org, 'Who Was Ludwig von Mises?' and the University of Vienna Memorial Book: he joined in 1909, served roughly twenty-five years, and eventually headed the finance department. Month and day unattested and defaulted. The coordinate is the dossier's pin for the Lower Austrian Chamber and was not independently re-geocoded.
stops.campa: He joins the Lower Austrian Chamber of Commerce and Industry as an economic adviser and remains about twenty-five years, ending as head of its finance department. Everything he does at the university is unpaid, and the memoranda on taxation, banking, currency, and trade that fill the next quarter century are written from a desk in a business lobby rather than a faculty office. The Chamber is what feeds him, and he acquires at that desk a working knowledge of Austrian fiscal machinery that no professor of the subject in the country possesses.
suggested_refs: The Kammer memoranda of Ludwig von Mises, 1909-1934, among the papers later seized and removed to Moscow

stops.name: Vienna, The Theory of Money and Credit
stops.date_confidence: Publication in 1912 attested by econlib.org's Concise Encyclopedia of Economics biography. Month and day unattested and defaulted. The pin is the Chamber office, where he was employed while writing it; no source consulted states where the book was written.
stops.campa: Theorie des Geldes und der Umlaufsmittel appears, written at thirty in the hours the Chamber leaves him. It carries marginal value theory into money itself, which the Austrians had left standing outside their own system as an awkward exception, and derives the purchasing power of a currency from the valuations of the individuals holding it rather than from any quantity a state decrees. In the last part the business cycle stops being weather. It becomes something banks manufacture by lending out money that nobody saved.
stops.quote: An economist must deal with doctrines, not with men. He must criticize erroneous thought.
stops.quote_source: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. V, 'First Writings on the Theory of Money'
sources: econlib.org, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, biography of Mises
Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition), Ch. V
suggested_refs: Theorie des Geldes und der Umlaufsmittel (Munich and Leipzig, 1912)

stops.name: University of Vienna, the lectureship that pays nothing
stops.date_confidence: Privatdozent from 1913 and the unpaid extraordinarius title from 1918 are both attested by the University of Vienna Memorial Book (gedenkbuch.univie.ac.at) and mises.org. Month and day for both are unattested; 1913 is used to order the segment and the 1918 title is folded into this stop rather than given its own. No source consulted states a reason for the absence of a paid chair.
stops.campa: He is admitted as Privatdozent, licensed to lecture and not to be paid for lecturing, and in 1918 is credited with the title of extraordinarius, an honorary associate professorship carrying the same nothing. On these terms he will teach at the University of Vienna for twenty-five years. The lectures are attended. There is no salary line to be cut. Neither the antisemitism of the faculty nor the unpopularity of his conclusions is ever entered anywhere as the reason, and no other reason is ever entered instead.
suggested_refs: University of Vienna habilitation file for Ludwig von Mises, 1913

segments.name: Field Artillery, and the Empire Coming Apart

stops.name: The Galician front, the Thirtieth Field Cannon Regiment
stops.date_confidence: Mobilization on 1 August 1914, service with Austro-Hungarian field artillery including the 30th Field Cannon Regiment, combat in Galicia and the Carpathians, later service in Russian Ukraine and Crimea, and the rank of captain are all carried from the dossier's First World War section, citing Hulsmann's biography and personnel records, none of which was fetched directly in this pass. The coordinate is a point on the Galician front, not a documented position.
stops.campa: Mobilized in the first days of August, he travels east toward the front that his birthplace sits behind, serving with Austro-Hungarian field artillery including the Thirtieth Field Cannon Regiment. The economist who will argue for the rest of his life that war is the enemy of the division of labor spends three years working guns across the province where he was born. He is in direct combat against Russian forces in Galicia and the Carpathians through two winters, later in Russian Ukraine and in the Crimea, and rises to captain.
sources: Dossier, First World War section, citing Jorg Guido Hulsmann, Mises: The Last Knight of Liberalism, and Austro-Hungarian personnel records
suggested_refs: Austro-Hungarian army personnel file for Ludwig von Mises, 30th Field Cannon Regiment

stops.name: The Stubenring, memoranda for a ministry with months left
stops.date_confidence: Transfer from front duty to economic staff work and the subject matter of the memoranda are carried from the dossier, which cites records recovered from Moscow; not independently verified. Month and day unattested and defaulted. Coordinate corrected: the k.u.k. Kriegsministerium occupied the Regierungsgebaude, Stubenring 1, 1010 Wien, from 1913 (48.2098, 16.3830, Nominatim); the dossier's 48.2044, 16.3679 lands near Karlsplatz and is wrong.
stops.campa: Pulled off front duty, he is set to writing in the Regierungsgebaude on the Stubenring: memoranda on inflation, war finance, currency, and trade for a War Ministry whose empire has a year and a half of existence left. He watches a currency destroyed by the government issuing it, from a desk inside the building doing the issuing. The papers he drafts here are among those the Gestapo will carry out of his apartment twenty-one years from now, and the Red Army will carry east to Moscow seven years after that.
sources: Dossier, First World War section, citing records recovered from the Moscow archive
University of Graz, Mises Private Archive project (privatarchiv-mises.uni-graz.at)
suggested_refs: Mises's war-finance memoranda for the k.u.k. Kriegsministerium, 1917-1918

stops.name: Vienna, the Settlements Office and the talk with Otto Bauer
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The directorship of the Austrian restitution-and-settlements office in 1918-1920 comes from the dossier; the claim that a private conversation with Otto Bauer helped dissuade a Bolshevik seizure of power rests on Mises's own recollection alone and the dossier flags it as such. No independent documentation has been produced by anyone. Month and day defaulted; the coordinate is the dossier's and was not re-geocoded.
stops.campa: In the wreck of the empire he directs a senior office administering financial settlements: reparations, currency conversion, the debts of a state that has ceased to exist, in a city where people are hungry and the Bolshevik example is eleven months old. He says afterward that a private conversation with Otto Bauer, his old seminar companion and now the strongest man in Austrian socialism, is what turned Bauer away from a seizure of power. Nobody has ever produced anything else that bears on it. Whether the conversation went as he remembered it, or carried the weight he gives it, the record has never been able to say.
stops.quote: It seemed incomprehensible to me that this garbled Hegelianism could exert such an enormous influence.
stops.quote_source: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. II, 'Etatism'
sources: Dossier, settlement work and revolutionary crisis section (tradition: Mises's own account)
Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition), Ch. II
suggested_refs: Mises's Notes and Recollections, on the Vienna of 1919 and Otto Bauer

stops.name: Vienna, the calculation article
stops.date_confidence: Attested: English Wikipedia's article on the economic calculation problem refers throughout to 'his 1920 article', Die Wirtschaftsrechnung im sozialistischen Gemeinwesen; Nation, Staat und Wirtschaft (1919) is standard bibliography. An earlier pass in this dossier recorded both as unconfirmed; that non-attestation is itself wrong and is corrected here. Month and day unattested and defaulted; the pin is his Chamber office.
stops.campa: He publishes Die Wirtschaftsrechnung im sozialistischen Gemeinwesen, an article that opens a debate still running a century later. Without private ownership of the means of production there are no prices for capital goods; without prices there is no arithmetic; without arithmetic a planning board cannot know whether building the steel mill is worth what the steel mill costs. It is not the argument that socialism will be unjust, or tyrannical, or inefficient. It is the argument that it cannot calculate. Nation, Staat und Wirtschaft had come the year before.
stops.quote: Money calculations of value will be impossible.
stops.quote_source: Socialism: An Economic and Sociological Analysis, trans. J. Kahane (Liberty Fund ed.), Part II, Ch. 7 'The Distribution of Income', section 4 'The Process of Distribution'
sources: Socialism, trans. J. Kahane (Liberty Fund ed.), Part II, Ch. 7
suggested_refs: Die Wirtschaftsrechnung im sozialistischen Gemeinwesen (Archiv fur Sozialwissenschaft und Sozialpolitik, 1920)

stops.name: The Herrengasse, the crown printed into nothing
stops.date_confidence: Advisory work on the reorganization of the Austrian National Bank and on the resolution of the Austrian hyperinflation in 1922 is attested by the University of Vienna Memorial Book. Month and day unattested and defaulted. Coordinate corrected: in 1922 the bank still occupied the former Austro-Hungarian Bank premises on the Herrengasse (approx. 48.2107, 16.3653); the purpose-built Otto-Wagner-Platz building (48.2163, 16.3544) was in use only from the mid-1920s.
stops.campa: The crown is being printed into nothing and Austrian savings are going with it. Mises advises on the reorganization of the Austrian National Bank, then still housed on the Herrengasse, and on the League of Nations stabilization that ends the inflation with a foreign loan and foreign supervision of Austrian finances. He is one adviser among the men working on it, and the legend that grows up afterward, that a single economist stopped the Austrian hyperinflation, compresses an international political operation into one man in one room.
suggested_refs: The 1922 Geneva Protocols and the League of Nations stabilization of Austrian finances

stops.name: Cafe Kunstler, the Friday circle
stops.date_confidence: The private seminar, its alternate-Friday schedule in Mises's Chamber office, its continuation at an Italian restaurant and then at the Cafe Kunstler, and the named regulars are all carried from the dossier's private-seminar section; the Memorial Book independently attests that his Vienna seminar drew Hayek. The date 1923 is an ordering device: the seminar ran across the 1920s and into 1934, and no start date is attested. The coordinate is the dossier's.
stops.campa: Every other Friday evening the private seminar meets in his office at the Chamber, and afterward moves to an Italian restaurant and then to the Cafe Kunstler, where the argument runs past midnight. Friedrich Hayek, Fritz Machlup, Oskar Morgenstern, Alfred Schutz, and Eric Voegelin are among the regulars: economists, lawyers, sociologists, phenomenologists. The man running the room holds no paid chair anywhere in the city, and the room itself is a business lobby's office and a coffee house. Nobody is enrolled in anything, nobody is graded, and nobody pays a fee.
stops.quote: What distinguishes the Austrian School and will lend it immortal fame is precisely the fact that it created a theory of economic action and not of economic equilibrium or non-action.
stops.quote_source: Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz), Ch. IV, 'The Austrian School of Economics'
sources: Dossier, private seminar and the Austrian network section
Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition), Ch. IV
suggested_refs: The Privatseminar of Ludwig von Mises, Vienna, 1920s to 1934

stops.name: New York, the first American tour
stops.date_confidence: The 1926 lecture and research tour funded by the Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial is carried from the dossier's travel section; month, day and itinerary are unattested and the date is defaulted. The coordinate is the generic New York City point, used because no venue is named in any source consulted.
stops.campa: Funded by the Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial, he crosses to the United States on a lecture and research tour, forty-four years old, looking at a country whose economists largely regard his position as a Viennese curiosity. He meets Americans and is met by them, and collects the addresses and the introductions that a European academic collects on such a trip and files away. Fourteen years later that list of names is what he will have to live on. No source consulted names a venue, a host, or a single date on the itinerary.
suggested_refs: Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial grant records for Mises's 1926 American tour

stops.name: Vienna, the Institute for Business Cycle Research
stops.date_confidence: Year corrected to 1927. English and German Wikipedia both give 1927 for the founding of the Osterreichisches Institut fur Konjunkturforschung by Mises with Hayek; econlib.org's biography says 1926, and the dossier carried both figures in different sections without reconciling them. The contradiction is recorded, not hidden. Month and day unattested and defaulted; the coordinate is the dossier's.
stops.campa: With Hayek he founds the Osterreichisches Institut fur Konjunkturforschung and installs his best student as its first director, aged twenty-eight. The institute does precisely what Mises's own method refuses to do: it counts things, month by month, and publishes empirical reports on the Austrian business cycle. Mises deduces from the proposition that men act. The institute measures. He builds it anyway, and it outlives the republic that houses it, the annexation, the war, and Mises himself. It is working in Vienna today under another name.
sources: econlib.org, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, biography of Mises (gives 1926)
Dossier, Institute for Business Cycle Research section
suggested_refs: The Osterreichisches Institut fur Konjunkturforschung, founded 1927, now the Austrian Institute of Economic Research

stops.name: Vienna, adviser to Chancellor Dollfuss
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The service as economic adviser to Engelbert Dollfuss is asserted by the Austria in USA cultural forum biography (austriainusa.org) and repeated in the dossier; no appointment document, memorandum, or contemporary record of what he advised was reached in this pass. Month and day unattested and defaulted. The pin is his Chamber office, not a chancellery room.
stops.campa: Engelbert Dollfuss suspends the Austrian parliament, rules by emergency decree, and builds a Catholic corporatist dictatorship braced against the Nazis on one side and the Social Democrats on the other. Mises serves him as an economic adviser. The man whose whole doctrine is that every extension of state compulsion is a subtraction from freedom takes a post with an authoritarian chancellor, on a calculation about which of the available regimes will do the least damage that he never set out at length in anything he published. What he actually advised is not on the record.
sources: Austria in USA cultural forum biography, austriainusa.org
suggested_refs: Austrian chancellery records of economic advice under Dollfuss, 1933-1934

stops.name: Geneva, the first salaried chair of his life
stops.date_confidence: Attested: the departure from Vienna on 3 October 1934 and the first Geneva lecture on 25 October are given in the dossier's Geneva section; the appointment itself is confirmed by econlib.org. Coordinate corrected to the Geneva Graduate Institute campus by the lake (46.2211, 6.1437, per Wikipedia's 46 13 15.8 N, 6 08 37.3 E); the dossier's 46.2044, 6.1432 is the city centre, about 1.9 km away.
stops.campa: William Rappard invites him to the Graduate Institute of International Studies, and on the third of October he leaves Vienna. Three weeks later he begins lecturing by the lake as professor of international economic relations. He is fifty-three, and this is the first regularly paid academic post of his life. He teaches in French, alongside Rappard, Paul Mantoux, and Hans Kelsen, who sat next to him under the Latin masters of the Akademisches Gymnasium forty-two years earlier. The Chamber desk and the Friday seminar are behind him for good.
sources: econlib.org, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, biography of Mises
suggested_refs: The Institut universitaire de hautes etudes internationales, Geneva, founded 1927 by Rappard and Mantoux

stops.name: Wollzeile, twenty-one boxes
stops.date_confidence: Attested that the Gestapo seized Mises's papers, library, correspondence, silver, paintings and coin collection from the Vienna apartment he had held since 1911 (FEE, Richard Ebeling, 'Mises's Lost Papers'; University of Graz Mises Private Archive project). Sources disagree on the day: English Wikipedia puts the raid on the day German forces entered Vienna, 12 March, while the dossier says days after, with twenty-one boxes removed in late March. Not reconciled. Coordinate corrected to Wollzeile 24 (48.2081, 16.3768).
stops.campa: German troops enter Vienna, and within days Nazi agents are inside the apartment on the Wollzeile that Mises had held since 1911 and left just before the annexation. He is in Geneva, lecturing in French, and will believe until the day he dies that all of it burned somewhere in the war. In late March they carry out twenty-one boxes, then come back for the rest: the library, the correspondence, the paintings, the silver, and a family coin collection of some hundred and fifty gold pieces and more than three thousand other coins and medals.
stops.quote: And now the peoples which have hailed with the greatest enthusiasm such writings, which call for the destruction of all cultural values, are themselves on the verge of a great social catastrophe.
stops.quote_source: Socialism: An Economic and Sociological Analysis, trans. J. Kahane (Liberty Fund ed.), Part V, Ch. 33, 'The Destructionism of the Literati'
sources: FEE, Richard Ebeling, 'Mises's Lost Papers: Plundered by the Nazis, Buried by the Soviets, Rediscovered by Me'
University of Graz, Mises Private Archive project (privatarchiv-mises.uni-graz.at)
suggested_refs: The Mises private archive: Vienna 1938, Moscow 1945-1996, Austrian State Archive from the early 2000s

stops.name: University of Vienna, struck from the roll
stops.date_confidence: The expulsion is attested by the University of Vienna Memorial Book, which the dossier reads as giving 22 April 1938 while other institutional pages give 8 April; the discrepancy is unresolved and 22 April is used here only to order the segment. The Memorial Book's own tagging of the entry is a reconstruction in the dossier's reading, not a quoted decree.
stops.campa: The University of Vienna strikes him from its roll of lecturers as a Jew, twenty-five years after admitting him and having paid him nothing across the whole of them. He is not in the country and does not contest it. There is no salary to stop, no office to vacate, no pension to cancel; the act removes a name from a list and the right to stand in a room. The university's own memorial records give two dates for it, the eighth of April and the twenty-second, and make no attempt to reconcile them.
sources: University of Vienna Memorial Book (gedenkbuch.univie.ac.at), Mises entry
suggested_refs: The University of Vienna Gedenkbuch for the dismissals of 1938

stops.name: Geneva, the marriage to Margit Serenyi
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction as to the exact day and place: mises.org attests the 1938 Geneva marriage, and the dossier gives 6 July 1938 at the Hotel de Ville with a courtship beginning at a Vienna dinner in 1925, drawing chiefly on Margit von Mises's own memoir. The coordinate is the Geneva Hotel de Ville and is the dossier's.
stops.campa: Ludwig von Mises and Margit Herzfeld Serenyi, a widowed actress, are married in Geneva. They met at a Vienna dinner in 1925, and the thirteen years between were consumed by her divorce, his mother, and his own long unwillingness, which she later wrote down without much softening it. He is fifty-six and has been driven out of the country where all of that happened. She will outlive him by twenty years, edit and defend what he leaves, and remain the only detailed witness to the two years that come next.
sources: Dossier, marriage and stepchildren section, citing Margit von Mises, My Years with Ludwig von Mises
suggested_refs: Margit von Mises, My Years with Ludwig von Mises

stops.name: Paris, the Colloque Walter Lippmann
stops.date_confidence: The colloquium and Mises's participation alongside Hayek, Ropke, Rustow, Lippmann and Rougier are carried from the dossier's Geneva section; the day is unattested and defaulted. The coordinate is the generic Paris centroid, used as an explicit fallback: the actual venue of the colloquium was not established in this pass, and a precise Paris address fixed for some unrelated event would be false precision here.
stops.campa: The participants gather in Paris around Walter Lippmann's book to ask whether liberalism can be rebuilt after its collapse. Hayek is there, and Wilhelm Ropke, Alexander Rustow, Louis Rougier, and Lippmann himself. The word neoliberalism is coined in the room. Mises holds the hardest position present: that the market requires no renovation whatever, and that the corrective interventions the others want are the disease being offered as its own cure. He argues the pure form of a doctrine whose impure defenders have just lost Europe.
suggested_refs: Compte-rendu des seances du Colloque Walter Lippmann, Paris, August 1938

stops.name: Geneva, Nationalokonomie and the papers for leaving
stops.date_confidence: Attested with unusual precision for the documents: the lawyer Pierre-Em. Atteslander's April 1940 request, the Swiss identity certificates delivered 31 May 1940, the Portuguese consulate's request of 5 June and Lisbon's authorization of 6 June are all from Procesos de Mercado, 'The Secret Passage: How Amzalak and Salazar Helped Ludwig von Mises Escape the Nazis' (2025). Nationalokonomie's 1940 Geneva publication by Editions Union is attested by the dossier and Wikipedia. The coordinate is the Geneva city point.
stops.campa: Nationalokonomie: Theorie des Handelns und Wirtschaftens is published in Geneva by Editions Union, a complete system built from first principles in German, and the war swallows its distribution nearly whole. In the same months his lawyer asks the Swiss authorities for identity certificates, because Mises will not travel any longer on a passport issued by Germany, and the Federal Police delivers them on the last day of May. On the fifth of June the Portuguese consulate wires Lisbon for an urgent transit visa. Lisbon authorizes it the following day.
sources: Procesos de Mercado, 'The Secret Passage: How Amzalak and Salazar Helped Ludwig von Mises Escape the Nazis' (2025)
suggested_refs: Swiss Federal Police and Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs files on the Mises transit visa, 1940

stops.name: Southern France, the road out
stops.date_confidence: Departure from Geneva on 4 July 1940 is attested in the dossier from Margit von Mises's memoir, which is the only detailed witness to the journey; later accounts do not agree on the means of transport or the road. The coordinate is a point in southern France (Toulouse) standing for a route that no source reconstructs day by day.
stops.campa: France has fallen and Switzerland is ringed. On the fourth of July the Miseses leave Geneva and work south and west by bus, by car, by whatever is moving, through a country in collapse with the German army settling in behind them. He is fifty-eight and carries a Swiss identity certificate, a Portuguese transit authorization, and a manuscript. Margit's memoir is the only account of this leg written by anyone who was on it, and the versions that came afterward do not agree with her or with each other.
sources: Dossier, escape from Europe section, citing Margit von Mises, My Years with Ludwig von Mises
suggested_refs: Margit von Mises, My Years with Ludwig von Mises, on the July 1940 journey

stops.name: The Spanish frontier, turned back and turned back again
stops.date_confidence: The repeated refusals at the Spanish frontier come from Margit von Mises's memoir alone, via the dossier; no day is attested and 10 July is an ordering device. Coordinate re-anchored: the dossier's 42.3667, 1.7833 sits in the high Pyrenees with no crossing used by 1940 refugees. Cerbere-Portbou (approx. 42.43, 3.16) is used as the Mediterranean-end crossing; the Atlantic-end alternative is Hendaye-Irun (approx. 43.35, -1.79). Which they actually used is not recorded.
stops.campa: At the Spanish frontier they are refused, and refused again, while the visas are argued over by men holding rubber stamps. Portugal has authorized the transit. Spain has not, and a border in July 1940 is a line where paper is read by officials with no professional interest whatever in an Austrian economist. They get across in the end. Whether it was at the Mediterranean end of the Pyrenees or the Atlantic end, no source consulted is able to say, and Margit, who was standing there, did not write it down.
sources: Dossier, escape from Europe section, citing Margit von Mises's memoir
suggested_refs: Spanish and Portuguese border transit records for refugees, July 1940

stops.name: Lisbon, the last open door in Europe
stops.date_confidence: Arrival in Lisbon and embarkation for America are attested in outline; the assistance of the Portuguese economist Moses Bensabat Amzalak and the Salazar government's documentation is from Procesos de Mercado (2025). No day of arrival or sailing is attested and 25 July is an ordering device between the 4 July departure and the 2 August landing. The coordinate is the Lisbon port point.
stops.campa: They reach Lisbon, which in the summer of 1940 is the last open door out of Europe and knows it. Moses Bensabat Amzalak, economist and head of the Portuguese Jewish community, works the Salazar government's paperwork on Mises's behalf. A berth westward is the scarcest commodity on the continent, and the queue outside every consulate in the city is measured in months rather than days. The Miseses get one. In early August the ship stands out of the Tagus.
sources: Procesos de Mercado, 'The Secret Passage: How Amzalak and Salazar Helped Ludwig von Mises Escape the Nazis' (2025)
suggested_refs: Moses Bensabat Amzalak's correspondence on the Mises transit, Lisbon 1940

stops.name: A New Jersey pier, Alfred Schutz waiting
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction as to the detail. Arrival in the United States in August 1940 with Rockefeller Foundation support is attested (mises.org; austriainusa.org). The 2 August date, the New Jersey pier, and Alfred Schutz meeting the ship come from the dossier alone, and no atlas file or independent source corroborates the Schutz detail. The coordinate is the dossier's.
stops.campa: They land at a New Jersey pier on the second of August, met by Alfred Schutz, who used to argue phenomenology against economists on Friday evenings in Vienna. Mises is a month short of fifty-nine and comes ashore with his wife and a manuscript. His library and his papers are gone into Germany and he does not know where. The language he wrote his life's work in is not the language of the profession here, no American university has offered him a chair, and the passage that brought him was paid for out of a foundation grant.
sources: Austria in USA cultural forum biography, austriainusa.org
suggested_refs: Rockefeller Foundation records of assistance to refugee scholars, 1940

stops.name: Harvard, Money as a Dynamic Factor
stops.date_confidence: The Harvard lecture on 'Money as a Dynamic Factor' in December 1940 and the American relationships formed around it (Hazlitt, Chamberlain, Eastman, Read, Fertig) are carried from the dossier's re-establishment section; the day is unattested and defaulted. The coordinate is the dossier's Harvard pin.
stops.campa: He lectures at Harvard on Money as a Dynamic Factor, in English, four months off the boat. The American economics profession is Keynesian and becoming more so by the term, and the men who will matter to Mises are almost none of them in it. The network that will pay for the next thirty years of his working life is forming instead out of journalists and businessmen: Henry Hazlitt of the New York Times, the critic John Chamberlain, Max Eastman coming across from communism, Leonard Read, Lawrence Fertig the advertising man.
sources: Dossier, re-establishment, grants, and Mexico section
suggested_refs: Mises's lecture 'Money as a Dynamic Factor', Harvard University, December 1940

stops.name: The National Bureau of Economic Research, a year on the payroll
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The guest-researcher position from 15 December 1940, the one-year term, and the Rockefeller-supported grant of 2,500 dollars come from the dossier's re-establishment section; no grant record or NBER document was reached in this pass. The Notes and Recollections sentence quoted here is attested as Mises's own, written in December 1940, via Margit von Mises's foreword to the Liberty Fund edition.
stops.campa: A Rockefeller-supported grant of twenty-five hundred dollars puts him on the payroll of the National Bureau of Economic Research for one year from the fifteenth of December. The Bureau measures: series, indices, cycles counted out of the data. Mises deduces from the single proposition that men act, and holds that no quantity of measurement settles anything about a cause. Neither side converts the other. What the appointment establishes is that he is employed in America, which in the winter of 1940 is the entirety of what he needs from it.
stops.quote: I set out to be a reformer, but only became the historian of decline.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig von Mises, written December 1940, quoted in Margit von Mises's foreword to Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund edition, trans. Hans F. Sennholz)
sources: Dossier, re-establishment, grants, and Mexico section
Notes and Recollections (Liberty Fund online edition), foreword by Margit von Mises

stops.name: 777 West End Avenue, apartment 3E
stops.date_confidence: The move into apartment 3E at 777 West End Avenue in October 1941 after a year of temporary lodging, and the couple's retention of the rent-regulated flat for life, are from the dossier. The day is unattested and defaulted. Coordinate corrected: 777 West End Avenue geocodes to 40.7966, -73.9725 (Nominatim), consistent with the West 98th Street cross street; the dossier's 40.7897, -73.9770 is roughly 800 m south.
stops.campa: After a year of temporary rooms they take apartment 3E at 777 West End Avenue, near Ninety-Eighth Street, a rent-regulated flat on the Upper West Side. They keep it for the rest of both their lives. He is fifty-nine, in his third country and his second working language, in an apartment reached by a lift in a building full of strangers who have no idea what he did in Vienna. Human Action is written at a desk in these rooms, and so is everything else he publishes from here on.
sources: Dossier, basic identifying information table and escape from Europe section

stops.name: Mexico City, lectures at the national university
stops.date_confidence: The 1942 visiting professorship and lectures at the National Autonomous University of Mexico are attested in the dossier, which however misattributed the resulting book. Corrected: the Mexico lectures were published as Problemas economicos de Mexico; Economic Policy: Thoughts for Today and Tomorrow is the 1959 Buenos Aires material (mises.org, Economic Policy library page). Month and day unattested and defaulted; the UNAM coordinate is confirmed.
stops.campa: Invited as a visiting professor, he lectures at the National Autonomous University in Mexico City, and comes back to lecture in the country again in later years. He is sixty years old, teaching in a third language to an audience in a state whose government is building its economy by plan. It is the first time since Vienna that a university has asked him to come and say in front of students what he thinks. The lectures appear in Spanish as Problemas economicos de Mexico.
sources: Dossier, re-establishment, grants, and Mexico section
suggested_refs: Ludwig von Mises, Problemas economicos de Mexico

stops.name: Trinity Place, the NYU seminar begins
stops.date_confidence: Attested: mises.org gives a visiting professorship at New York University from February 1945 to May 1969, and the dossier adds the Trinity Place commerce campus, the William Volker Fund salary, and the later Fertig consortium. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from murray_rothbard.journey.json, which pins the same room at 40.7079, -74.0138; it was not re-geocoded here. The day is unattested and defaulted.
stops.campa: He begins teaching at New York University, in the business school on Trinity Place a few streets from the Stock Exchange, because no economics department in America will house him. The title is visiting professor and NYU contributes nothing toward it: the William Volker Fund pays the salary, and later a consortium of businessmen assembled by Lawrence Fertig. He is sixty-three and holds at last a standing seminar inside a university building, on other men's money. He will hold it for twenty-four years.
stops.quote: It is an essential feature of socialistic methods of production that the shares of the different factors of production in the result cannot be ascertained.
stops.quote_source: Socialism: An Economic and Sociological Analysis, trans. J. Kahane (Liberty Fund ed.), Part II, Ch. 7 'The Distribution of Income', section 3; quoted here from mid-sentence in the original
suggested_refs: William Volker Fund records of the NYU visiting professorship, 1945-1969

stops.name: Irvington-on-Hudson, the Foundation for Economic Education
stops.date_confidence: Attested that Mises advised FEE from 1946 until his death, was placed on its payroll in its first year, and that FEE published his Planned Chaos (dossier, FEE section). United States citizenship in 1946 is attested by mises.org and econlib.org, with no courthouse or date detail found; it is folded into this stop rather than pinned to a generic city point. Month and day unattested and defaulted.
stops.campa: Leonard Read founds the Foundation for Economic Education in a house at Irvington-on-Hudson, up the river from the city, and puts Mises on its payroll in the first year. Adviser is the word, and it means that his name and his arguments belong to the operation while most of his time does not. FEE publishes Planned Chaos. The relation holds for twenty-seven years, until he dies: patronage rather than employment, a doctrine rather than a job. The same year, at sixty-four, he becomes an American citizen.
sources: Dossier, Foundation for Economic Education section
econlib.org, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, biography of Mises

stops.name: Mont Pelerin, the Hotel du Parc
stops.date_confidence: Attested: English Wikipedia's Mont Pelerin Society article gives the founding meeting at the Hotel du Parc, Mont Pelerin near Vevey, 10 April 1947, with thirty-nine participants. Coordinate corrected to Mont Pelerin, Chardonne, Vaud (46.4969, 6.8193, Wikipedia and Nominatim); the dossier's 46.4550, 6.8564 lands near Chexbres. The walkout is a separate matter, flagged in the campa: it is Milton Friedman's recollection, related by the Hoover Institution, of this or a later meeting, and is not a verified verbatim exchange.
stops.campa: Hayek gathers thirty-nine people at the Hotel du Parc on Mont Pelerin above Vevey, in the Switzerland Mises had to leave through the back door seven years earlier, to found a society for the defense of a doctrine with almost no defenders left alive in Europe. Mises holds the oldest position in the room and the strictest one. Milton Friedman remembered him rising in the middle of an argument about progressive taxation, telling the assembled company they were a pack of socialists, and walking out. Friedman was recalling it decades afterward.
stops.quote: Those who are asking for more government interference are asking ultimately for more compulsion and less freedom.
stops.quote_source: Human Action: A Treatise on Economics (Yale University Press, 1949), Part Six, Ch. XXVII, 'The Government and the Market', section 2

Human Action, Ch. XXVII (econlib.org full text)

stops.name: New Haven, Human Action
stops.date_confidence: The 1949 Yale University Press first edition is attested (Open Library record; English Wikipedia, 'Human Action'), and Eugene Davidson's role as editor is from the dossier. The day, 14 September, is carried from the dossier and could not be independently confirmed in sources reachable here; the year is not in doubt. The earlier dossier tag of [R] on this publication was wrong and is corrected to attested.
stops.campa: Yale University Press publishes Human Action: A Treatise on Economics, pushed through by the editor Eugene Davidson against a house with no obvious reason to want it. He is sixty-seven and writing in his second language. It is not a translation of the Geneva Nationalokonomie but a rebuilding of it in English: from the axiom that men act toward chosen ends by chosen means, outward through exchange, money, credit, the cycle, and the whole apparatus of intervention.
stops.quote: A 'chocolate king' has no power over the consumers, his patrons. He provides them with chocolate of the best possible quality and at the cheapest price. The consumers are not tied to him. They are free to stop patronizing his shops. He loses his 'kingdom' if the consumers prefer to spend their pennies elsewhere.
stops.quote_source: Human Action: A Treatise on Economics (New Haven: Yale University Press, 1949), Part Four, Ch. XV, on the metaphorical employment of the terminology of political rule
sources: Open Library record for Human Action (first published 1949, Yale University Press)
Human Action, Ch. XV (econlib.org full text)

stops.name: Trinity Place, Rothbard comes to the seminar
stops.date_confidence: Attendance and the 1949 trigger are attested in murray_rothbard.journey.json, which dates his first attendance 1949-09-01; since Human Action appeared in mid-September, October is used here purely to keep this file's segment in chronological order, and the discrepancy is deliberate and noted. The 1962 commendation of Man, Economy, and State and the anarchism split are likewise attested in Rothbard's file. Pin inherited byte-identical from that file.
stops.campa: A twenty-three-year-old named Murray Rothbard reads Human Action when it appears and starts coming to the Trinity Place seminar, a room that holds graduate students, businessmen, and outright cranks. He comes for years and calls Mises his teacher for the rest of his life; by that first winter he is already arguing that the logic requires anarchism, and Mises never accepts a word of it from him or from anyone. In 1962, at eighty-one, Mises reads Rothbard's Man, Economy, and State and commends it in writing.
sources: murray_rothbard.journey.json, stop 'NYU School of Commerce, the seminar of Ludwig von Mises'

segments.name: The Late Honors, and the Grave

stops.name: Grove City College, the honorary doctorate
stops.date_confidence: The 1957 honorary LL.D. is confirmed by English Wikipedia; the route through his student Hans Sennholz and the later custody of some 20,000 pages of Mises papers are from the dossier and Wikipedia. The Freiburg honorary doctorate in political science (1964) and the NYU honorary doctorate (1963) are attested in the dossier's awards section and are folded into this stop rather than given pins of their own. Coordinate corrected to 41.1553, -80.0787 (Nominatim). Month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: Grove City College in western Pennsylvania gives him an honorary Doctor of Laws, arranged through his student Hans Sennholz, who teaches there. New York University will follow with an honorary doctorate in 1963, and Freiburg with a doctorate in political science in 1964. Every one of these arrives from an institution that never carried him on a faculty payroll, and two of them from institutions that employed him without paying him. Grove City will end up holding some twenty thousand pages of his papers and unpublished work.
suggested_refs: The Mises collection at Grove City College, Pennsylvania

stops.name: Buenos Aires, six lectures at the university
stops.date_confidence: Attested by mises.org's Economic Policy library page: the six lectures were delivered at the University of Buenos Aires in 1959, later written up in prose, and published by Regnery in 1979 with a Free Market Books edition in 1995. The dossier missed this journey entirely and attached the resulting book to the 1942 Mexico trip instead. Month, day and venue are unattested; the coordinate is the Buenos Aires city point, and the university building is not identified in the source.
stops.campa: He gives six lectures at the University of Buenos Aires, seventy-seven years old, in an Argentina four years past the fall of Peron and arguing loudly with itself about what a state is for. He speaks on capitalism, socialism, interventionism, inflation, foreign investment, and politics, without a text in front of him. It is the last body of work he makes from a lectern, and he makes it in South America. The lectures are taken down and written up in prose afterward, and published twenty years later, after his death, as Economic Policy: Thoughts for Today and Tomorrow.
sources: mises.org, Economic Policy: Thoughts for Today and Tomorrow, library page
suggested_refs: Ludwig von Mises, Economic Policy: Thoughts for Today and Tomorrow (Regnery/Gateway, 1979), from the Buenos Aires lectures of 1959

stops.name: Chicago, Regnery repairs the botched edition
stops.date_confidence: Attested that Yale's 1963 revised edition of Human Action was defective and had to be reprinted (English Wikipedia, 'Human Action'), that Mises called it a scandalous botchery (dossier, Human Action section), and that Henry Regnery issued a corrected third edition in 1966. Month and day unattested and defaulted; the coordinate is the generic Chicago point, the Regnery office address not being established here.
stops.campa: Yale reissues Human Action in 1963 in an edition so badly set that Mises calls it a scandalous botchery, and Margit fights the press about it while another printing is rushed out. The book is selling to a readership that grew while the profession he belongs to was looking somewhere else entirely. Henry Regnery takes it to Chicago and produces a corrected third edition, the third publisher the treatise has had in seventeen years. The author is eighty-five, reading proofs on a book he began building in Geneva in 1940.
suggested_refs: Henry Regnery Company third edition of Human Action, Chicago, 1966

stops.name: Trinity Place, the last seminar
stops.date_confidence: The end of the NYU visiting professorship in May 1969 is attested by mises.org and the dossier's NYU section; the day is unattested and defaulted. Pin inherited byte-identical from murray_rothbard.journey.json.
stops.campa: In May he takes the NYU seminar for the last time, eighty-seven years old, twenty-four years after the first session in this building. The men who sat in this room will spend the rest of their careers arguing with each other about what he meant. He has taught in Vienna without pay for a quarter century, in Geneva in French for six years, and in New York for twenty-four on money raised from businessmen, and has never in his life held an ordinary salaried chair in economics anywhere.
suggested_refs: The NYU Mises seminar, 1945-1969, and the students who passed through it

stops.name: 777 West End Avenue, the death
stops.date_confidence: Death on 10 October 1973 in New York City at age 92 is attested by the University of Vienna Memorial Book, mises.org, and English Wikipedia. That he died in the West End Avenue apartment is inferred from the dossier's statement that the couple kept it for life and is not separately documented. No public source consulted gives a cause of death. Coordinate corrected to 40.7966, -73.9725.
stops.campa: Ludwig von Mises dies at ninety-two in New York, in the apartment on West End Avenue the couple took in 1941. He has outlived the Habsburg empire, the Austrian republic that replaced it, the corporate state that replaced that, the Vienna he was raised in, and every one of the men who sat around Bohm-Bawerk's table. His own papers, which he believed had burned in the war, are at this moment in a locked archive in Moscow, twenty-three years from being found. No public source consulted gives a cause of death.
suggested_refs: Margit von Mises, My Years with Ludwig von Mises, on the last years

stops.name: Ferncliff, Hartsdale
stops.date_confidence: Burial at Ferncliff Cemetery, Hartsdale, Westchester County is attested by English Wikipedia; the date of interment is unattested and 13 October is an ordering device. Coordinate corrected to 41.0275, -73.8322 (Wikipedia, 41 01 39 N 73 49 56 W); the dossier carried two different wrong pins for the same cemetery. The Hillsdale bequest, the Ebeling recovery in October 1996, and the Austrian restitution are attested by English Wikipedia, FEE (Ebeling's own account), and the University of Graz project page respectively.
stops.campa: He is buried at Ferncliff Cemetery in Hartsdale, in Westchester County north of the city, among the twentieth century's other New York arrivals. His personal library goes by his will to Hillsdale College in Michigan. In October 1996 Richard Ebeling and his wife Anna find the Vienna papers in a former Soviet secret archive in Moscow, sealed there by Stalin's order since 1945, and spend ten days photocopying nearly ten thousand pages; the originals go back to Austria in the early 2000s. No plaque, statue, or street in Vienna carries his name that anyone has been able to find.
sources: FEE, Richard Ebeling, 'Mises's Lost Papers: Plundered by the Nazis, Buried by the Soviets, Rediscovered by Me'
University of Graz, Mises Private Archive project (privatarchiv-mises.uni-graz.at)
